One worker can do jobs in order. Several workers can work at the same time, but they must not fight over the same notebook.

How to test this example in Visual Studio

Download the project below, extract it into its own folder, then open StudyLab.csproj. Wait for NuGet restore. Choose Build → Build Solution. For console projects choose Start Without Debugging. For API projects use View → Terminal, make sure the terminal is in the folder containing StudyLab.csproj, then run the command shown in the lesson. Do not paste all files into Program.cs: use the exact file names displayed below.

Make shared updates safe

int count = 0;
Parallel.For(0, 1000, _ => Interlocked.Increment(ref count));
Console.WriteLine($"Safe count: {count}");
var worker = new Thread(() => Console.WriteLine("Worker thread finished"));
worker.Start();
worker.Join();

Expected count: 1000. count++ reads, adds and writes, so racing workers can lose updates. Interlocked makes this small update atomic. lock protects a larger critical section; keep locks short. Join waits for a thread to finish and blocks the caller.

Choose the right model

  • Multithreading: more than one thread can make progress.
  • Parallelism: work executes at the same time, useful for sufficiently large CPU calculations. Task.Run can offload CPU work from a desktop UI thread.
  • Asynchrony: do not block while waiting for I/O. It can use the same thread again later; async does not always create a new thread.
  • WPF controls belong to their UI thread. Use Dispatcher for UI updates from another thread. Never share a DbContext across parallel tasks; give independent work separate scopes or contexts.

Try it yourself

Why is a static List dangerous for simultaneous API writes?

Worked answer

Concurrent mutation can corrupt assumptions. Use a real database, a properly locked store, or a suitable concurrent collection for an in-memory demo.

When is Parallel.For a bad choice?

Worked answer

For tiny jobs or waiting on network I/O, overhead or blocked workers can make it slower.
